title.en: A Friend Found in Music: a poem by Bryanna T. Perkins

text.en: Some friends never speak yet always seem to understand. For the poet, that friend is music.

A Friend Found in Music is a short poem by Bryanna T. Perkins about what music means to the speaker.
It begins with metaphors. Music is described as the ocean that pulls the speaker to the shore and as the rhythm that moves the speaker to the core.
The line pattern repeats the words music is again and again. This repetition at the start of lines is called anaphora.
Music is also called therapy for the blues. When the speaker feels low, music lifts the spirits and helps them pull through.
When the speaker is cheerful, music was there too, so music accompanies both joy and sorrow.
The last lines call music the needed friend when no one seems to care. Music becomes a companion in loneliness.
The poem has an easy, musical rhyme: the second and fourth lines of each stanza rhyme, such as blue and through, and there and care.
The mood is hopeful and comforting, and the theme is that music supports us emotionally in every mood.

problem.en: Show how repetition and rhyme help the poem sound like music.

text.en: The words music is begin many lines.
Blue rhymes with through and there with care.
Together they give a regular, song-like beat.

prompt.en: Why does the poet call music a friend?

requiredIdeas.en: It is with us in happy times
It is there when no one seems to care

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking music only helps in happy moments

points.en: The poem by Bryanna T. Perkins shows music as a friend and therapy.
Alternate lines rhyme, giving a song-like beat.
The mood is hopeful and comforting.
